rv.q: Happily, the spell that this smaller-scale War of the Worlds casts lingers long after the small company have taken their bows.

The beauty of this particular production, as Bradberry states, is that the live actors are a total of 5500 miles away from each other—in Chicago, New Orleans, and Vancouver, Canada—and can seamless bridge this distance through the magic of (video) conferencing.

cn.t: Critics find this stage adaptation of Orson Welles' iconic broadcast a timely, thought-provoking experience, praised for its media literacy themes. Reception is generally positive, though not without reservations.
